builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Gragas: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (1,042 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 51.9% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A melee control mage who alternates defensive drinking and empowered attacks with dashes and precise displacement. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Rod of Ages → Fimbulwinter → Cosmic Drive. Stormraider's Surge keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Zhonya's Hourglass, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Rod of Ages → Fimbulwinter → Cosmic Drive, with Stormraider's Surge.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Rod of Ages → Fimbulwinter → Cosmic Drive) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 51.9% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Rod of Ages → Fimbulwinter → Cosmic Drive.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

builds.name: Drunken spellblade tank
builds.summary: Trade one-shot burst for repeated protected empowered attacks.
builds.goal: Trade one-shot burst for repeated protected empowered attacks.
builds.hypothesis: Drunken Rage reduces damage with an AP term and empowers one attack with 0.7 AP plus 7% enemy max-health magic damage. Dusk and Dawn adds a separate attack proc, Riftmaker rewards continued combat, and Visage supports Happy Hour's 5.5% max-health heal. Body Slam's collision reduces its cooldown by 40%, helping create another W window.
testPlan: Required state: Need E collisions, W timing before contact and Happy Hour availability.
Compare W-hit damage, passive healing and E availability across two exchanges at equal gold.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Missing E loses the cooldown reduction; W's short protection can expire while chasing.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: W's percent-health magic bonus does not multiply separate on-hit item damage.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Dusk and Dawn, Riftmaker, Spirit Visage, Abyssal Mask, Cosmic Drive, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Magic matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Gragas: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A melee control mage who alternates defensive drinking and empowered attacks with dashes and precise displacement. Measure empowered W attacks after drinking, E access and R displacement. A bruiser route must compare survival and repeat casts rather than assume the burst combo always lands. MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
builds.summary: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Gragas: Measure empowered W attacks after drinking, E access and R displacement. A bruiser route must compare survival and repeat casts rather than assume the burst combo always lands.

Start with the early core (Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Gragas rolls his cask to a location, which can be activated to explode or will explode on its own after 4 seconds. The potency of the explosion increases over time. Enemies struck by the blast have their Move Speed slowed. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.

The route fails Gragas's stated kit question: Measure empowered W attacks after drinking, E access and R displacement. A bruiser route must compare survival and repeat casts rather than assume the burst combo always lands.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.
Full cost 15,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Abyssal Mask, Spirit Visage, Jak'Sho, The Protean are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.

builds.name: Fermented barrel displacement
builds.summary: Use a held barrel and R placement to create a larger delayed hit.
builds.goal: Use a held barrel and R placement to create a larger delayed hit.
builds.hypothesis: Barrel Roll's 0.8 AP magic damage rises up to 1.5 times as it ages over four seconds. Explosive Cask's 0.8 AP knockback can displace a target toward the prepared barrel; Rocketbelt adjusts the casting angle, while Horizon reveals qualifying long-range ability hits. This is a placement-dependent damage hypothesis rather than an automatic combo.
testPlan: Required state: Need an aged barrel, a displacement angle and safe range for setup.
Measure aged-Q damage and successful R-into-Q catches against a moving target, logging range for Horizon.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: A wrong R angle ejects the enemy away; detonating Q early sacrifices its multiplier.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Every Q detonation is not the full aged damage, and Horizon does not amplify all spells in this source.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.

Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
